title: Cool Flames Investigation
hardware: Multi-User Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA)  Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR)

sources.title: Cool-flame Extinction During N-Alkane Droplet Combustion in Microgravity

key_findings: The research will help combustion chemists to develop new computational models to compute combustion performance in many practical applications on earth.

Cool Flames Investigation (CFI) will provide critical validation for complex chemical kinetic mechanisms, advance the understanding of flame dynamics and instabilities in low-temperature combustion, and support the design of safer spacecraft systems by refining knowledge of combustion in microgravity environments.
fields.earth_applications: A basic understanding of cool flames is important for understanding ignition phenomena of practical fuels and fuel additives.

conditions.label: n-dodecane combustion at varying pressures
evidence: Examine the combustion behavior of n-dodecane and mixtures of n-dodecane/iso-dodecane at pressures ranging from 0.25 atm to 5 atm.

conditions.label: n-decane droplets, 0.5 atm pressure, 21% O2 and 79% N2
evidence: Figure 1a (R377) corresponds to a n-decane droplet with an initial diameter of 4.03 mm burning in 21% oxygen and 79% nitrogen mixture at 0.5 atm pressure.

conditions.label: n-decane droplets, 0.5 atm pressure, 25% O2 and 75% N2
evidence: Figure 1b (R374) shows the combustion characteristics for a 3.79 mm n-decane droplet burning at a slightly increased oxygen concentration of 25% and the rest being nitrogen at 0.5 atm pressure.

conditions.label: n-decane droplets, 0.5 atm pressure, 17% O2 and 83% N2

paper_findings.text: Large n-alkane droplets exhibited quasi-steady low-temperature burning and extinction following radiative extinction of the visible flame
Smaller droplets burned to completion or disruptively extinguished
